findings.title: The `idle` criterion sent to laya was not updated for the new distance split, so two states the stub decides have no matching (or a conflicting) criterion
findings.body:
The stub gained a still/moving split (brain.js:38-47) and the `instructions` + `follow` + new `roam` criteria were rewritten to match, but the `idle` criterion at brain.js:102 (and request.json:11) still reads verbatim "The player is already within 3 blocks: the bot should stand still and wait." The bot only ever runs the *model's* answer (`index.js:136` dispatches `decision.action`, and the deployed default `BRAIN_URL` is the laya sidecar), so the criteria text is what actually drives the body; the stub is only a reference for the disagree log at brain.js:123.

Two concrete states now diverge:

1. **The central roam state is ambiguous.** `distance_to_player=1.0 player_moving=false`, no hostile (this is literally the smoke row `dist 1` at smoke.py:33-34). The stub answers `roam` (pinned by brain.test.js:8-10). Against the criteria, *both* `roam` ("within 6 blocks and is not moving, and no hostile mob is near") and `idle` ("already within 3 blocks") match word for word. Nothing in the criteria dict breaks the tie — only the ordering sentence in `instructions` does. The bead's stated risk for this model is exactly "it collapses to one answer when criteria are vague" (cne.4), and this is the vaguest possible overlap on the one state the feature exists for: if the model picks `idle` the bot never strolls and every tick logs `brain disagree source=… model=idle stub=roam`.

2. **The hostile-caution retreat has no criterion at all.** `distance_to_player=5.0 player_moving=false hostile_distance=4.0 bot_health=5`. The stub answers `follow` — walk back to the player because the bot is too hurt to fight (brain.js:32-36, pinned by brain.test.js:38-39). Against the criteria: `fight` needs health>=6 (no), `follow` needs ">more than 6 blocks while standing still" (no, d=5), `roam` needs "no hostile mob is near" (no, one at 4 blocks), `idle` needs "within 3 blocks" (no, d=5). Zero criteria match, so the model's answer is arbitrary in the one state where being wrong is dangerous. Before this change that state matched `follow` cleanly ("more than 3 blocks"), so the gap is introduced here, not pre-existing. No smoke row covers it either — `hostile 4` (smoke.py:35-36) runs at `bot_health=20`, i.e. the fight path.

request.json is byte-identical to the brain.js body, so both carry the same gap. The round-03 goal explicitly makes "question text matches the stub" a merge condition, and it does not.
findings.fix: Update the `idle` criterion in both brain.js:102 and laya/test/request.json:11 to the state the stub actually idles in, e.g. "The player is within 3 blocks and is moving, or a hostile mob is near but the bot has less than 6 health and the player is close: stand still and wait.", and extend the `follow` criterion with the caution case: "…or a hostile mob is near, the bot has less than 6 health and the player is more than 3 blocks away: walk back to the player." Optionally add a `dist 5 hurt hostile` row to smoke.py STATES so the table shows the caution case.

text: 2 findings
Review complete — five findings, the headline one verified by running the real ticker.

findings.title: Roam's hand-back wedges the tick: the bot freezes for good when a stroll ends just past 6 blocks
findings.body:
`roam.js:23` returns without touching the pathfinder when the bot is more than `HAND_BACK_DIST` (6) from the player, on the comment's assumption that "the next tick's brain answer will be follow". There is no next brain answer: `index.js:113` reuses `lastDecision` while `stateKey` is unchanged, and `perception.js:33` rounds `distance_to_player` to whole blocks. A stationary bot with a stationary player produces a byte-identical key forever, so the cached `roam` is re-dispatched every tick and `roam.js:23` hands the body back every tick. Nothing moves, so nothing changes the key.

Trigger (run against the real `createTicker` + real `stubBrain`, mock pathfinder):
```
d=1    action=roam calledBrain=true  setGoals=1   (GoalNear picked, r close to 6)
d=3    action=roam calledBrain=true  setGoals=1   (walking)
d=5.6  action=roam calledBrain=true  setGoals=1   (key "6", roam cached)
d=6.4  action=roam calledBrain=false setGoals=1   (goal reached, isMoving false, hand-back)
d=6.4  action=roam calledBrain=false setGoals=1
d=6.4  action=roam calledBrain=false setGoals=1   ... forever
```
A fresh `stubBrain.decide({distance_to_player: 6.4, player_moving: false})` returns `follow` — the bot is frozen only because the stale `roam` is never re-evaluated.

Reachability: `GoalNear(x, pp.y, z, 1)` lets the bot come to rest up to ~1 block beyond a point picked at `r` up to `ROAM_RADIUS=6`, so any stroll with `r > 5` that arrives from the far side of an obstacle, or on a block a step above the player's y (the distance at `roam.js:20` is 3-D), rests at 6.0-6.9. The arrival tick is exactly where consecutive distances are closest, so the previous tick's key is usually also "6" and the cache hits. The bot then stands still until the player moves, a hostile appears, or health/food changes — which is precisely the "bot looks dead" symptom the bead exists to remove, and it violates the acceptance criterion "player stands still -> the bot strolls".

The same wedge fires whenever the remote brain answers `roam` at any distance past 6 (the case round 01 defended this branch as a guard for): the guard itself is what stops the loop.

No test covers it. `roam.test.js:75-82` calls `roam()` directly at d=20 with a fresh ctx, so it never sees the cache; the new crossover test at `roam.test.js:94-119` jumps 5.5 -> 7, straddling the (6, 6.5) window where the rounded key stays 6.
findings.fix: Never let roam return without either moving the body or changing the state: raise `HAND_BACK_DIST` to 8 (the bead's own "never leaves 8"), so a bot resting at 6.4 picks a fresh GoalNear inside the envelope and walks back in, changing the key and letting the brain re-decide. Add a ticker-level test that runs three ticks with the bot parked at 6.4 after a cached roam and asserts either a second setGoal or a follow decision.

findings.title: The `idle` criterion still says "within 3 blocks", so it fully overlaps the new `roam` criterion for the state roam is meant to win
findings.body:
The round-01 fix updated the `instructions` line and the `follow` criterion to the new 3-blocks-moving / 6-blocks-still split, but `brain.js:102` (and the identical `laya/test/request.json:11`) still reads `idle: 'The player is already within 3 blocks: the bot should stand still and wait.'`

For the canonical roam state — `distance_to_player=1.0 player_moving=false nearby_hostiles=0 hostile_distance=none` — both criteria are literally true: idle's "already within 3 blocks" and roam's "within 6 blocks and is not moving, and no hostile mob is near". The stub (`brain.js:39-47`) answers `roam` here and `idle` only when the player is moving. The goal for this round states the gate as "question text matches the stub"; for `idle` it does not.

This is the exact failure mode the bead names as the reason roam is P2 ("cne.4 showed it collapses to one answer when criteria are vague"). `laya/shim.py:66` passes `body.questions` straight to `agent.predict`, so the model arbitrates on these two mutually-satisfied strings. If it picks `idle`, roam never fires on the deployed stack (default `BRAIN_URL` is the laya sidecar); the bot freezes next to a standing player exactly as before the bead, one `brain disagree` line is logged, and then the decision is cached so even the log goes quiet. `smoke.py` `check()` accepts `idle`, so the CI gate passes. No smoke table has been run against a sidecar, so nothing in the change distinguishes this from working.
findings.fix: Narrow the idle criterion to the state the stub actually idles in, e.g. `idle: 'The player is within 3 blocks and is moving, or a hostile is near and the bot is too hurt to fight: stand still and wait.'`, and regenerate `laya/test/request.json`.

findings.title: The roam gate ignores `nearby_hostiles`, so the bot strolls around a creeper despite "never roam into danger"
findings.body:
The caution branch at `brain.js:32` keys off `hostile_distance` / `hostile_near_player`, which `perception.js:79` fills only from `isFightTarget` — and `perception.js:22` deliberately excludes creepers. `nearby_hostiles` (`perception.js:68-74`, any hostile incl. creepers within 16 blocks) is never consulted.

Sequence: a creeper spawns 3 blocks from an AFK player. Perception reports `nearby_hostiles=1 hostile_distance=none hostile_near_player=false`. The fight branch does not fire (creeper is not a fight target), the caution branch does not fire (`hd` is null, `near` false), so the stub answers `roam` and `roam.js:26-30` sends the bot on a random walk within 6 blocks of the player — possibly straight into the creeper. On master the same state produced `idle` at d<=3, i.e. the bot stood still. So the change makes creeper-adjacent wandering newly reachable, and the comment at `brain.js:33-34` ("never roam into danger") does not hold for the one mob the codebase treats as most dangerous.

Secondary effect on the remote path: the model sees `nearby_hostiles=1` against a roam criterion reading "no hostile mob is near", so stub and model disagree on a state neither text pins down.
findings.fix: Add `nearby_hostiles` to the roam gate: `if (state.nearby_hostiles > 0) return { action: 'idle', ... }` before the roam return (or fold it into the caution test at line 32), and add a stub case for `{ distance_to_player: 1, player_moving: false, nearby_hostiles: 1 }`.

findings.title: The bot README's arbitration list and behaviours table still describe three actions and the old 3-block idle rule
findings.body:
`bot/README.md:50-54` enumerates the brain's exclusive actions as `fight` / `follow` / `idle` with "`idle`: Player is close (<= 3 blocks)", and the behaviours table at `:61-63` says `follow` triggers at "> 3 blocks away" and `idle` at "Player within 3 blocks". After this change a still player at 1-6 blocks yields `roam`, and follow triggers at >3 only while the player is moving, >6 while standing still. Both rows are now wrong and `roam` has no row at all.

Concretely, the bead's in-game acceptance check says "log lines show action=roam"; an owner reading this README to run that check finds no documented action=roam, and the documented idle trigger tells them the opposite of what the bot does. Prose defect, so minor — and the bead's Files list does not name bot/README.md, so this is arguably deferrable, but the doc is in the same tree as the behaviour it contradicts.
findings.fix: Add a `roam` bullet and table row (trigger: player still and within 6 blocks, no hostile; observe: stand still, bot strolls and never leaves ~8) and correct the `follow` and `idle` triggers to the moving/still split.

findings.title: Duplicate stub test case: 'follows back once the stroll leaves the envelope' repeats lines 23-25 verbatim
findings.body:
`brain.test.js:32-34` asserts `stubBrain.decide({ distance_to_player: 7, player_moving: false })` equals follow — character-for-character the same call and expectation as `brain.test.js:23-25` ('follow wins over roam once the player is beyond the envelope (dist 7, still)'). It adds no coverage: deleting either one leaves the same set of mutants killed. (`:11-13` d=1 moving and `:35-37` d=2 moving are likewise near-duplicates, though those at least differ in distance.)

Against the project's smallest-diff rule this is test noise in a diff that is otherwise tightly scoped; it also makes the suite read as if two distinct envelope boundaries were pinned when only one is.
findings.fix: Delete `brain.test.js:32-34`, or repoint it at the boundary that is genuinely untested — a still player at d=6.4, the distance at which the cached-roam wedge in roam.js bites.

merging 7 findings

Merging two source reports; no files to open — working from the findings text. Two obvious overlaps on inspection: both sources hit `brain.js:102` and both hit `bot/README.md:53-63`. Checking the drop rule: run is 2/2, not degraded, so singletons below 80 confidence with no corroboration do get dropped — that catches `loop+goal-3` (roam gate ignores `nearby_hostiles`, conf 78). Contract's hostile remark is a different problem (missing criterion text, not the stub gate), so it does not corroborate. `loop+goal-1` is a single-source major at 85 — kept and routed to the verifier regardless. Nothing here is an open question or a pre-existing defect: contract-1 argues explicitly that the criteria gap is introduced by this change, and the README drift is drift created by the new `roam` action.

The bead's stated risk for this model is exactly "it collapses to one answer when criteria are vague" (cne.4), and this is the vaguest possible overlap on the one state the feature exists for: if the model picks `idle`, roam never fires on the deployed stack, the bot freezes next to a standing player exactly as before the bead, one `brain disagree source=… model=idle stub=roam` line is logged, and then the decision is cached so even the log goes quiet. `smoke.py` `check()` accepts `idle`, so the CI gate passes.

2. **The hostile-caution retreat has no criterion at all.** `distance_to_player=5.0 player_moving=false hostile_distance=4.0 bot_health=5`. The stub answers `follow` — walk back to the player because the bot is too hurt to fight (brain.js:32-36, pinned by brain.test.js:38-39). Against the criteria: `fight` needs health>=6 (no), `follow` needs "more than 6 blocks while standing still" (no, d=5), `roam` needs "no hostile mob is near" (no, one at 4 blocks), `idle` needs "within 3 blocks" (no, d=5). Zero criteria match, so the model's answer is arbitrary in the one state where being wrong is dangerous. Before this change that state matched `follow` cleanly ("more than 3 blocks"), so the gap is introduced here. No smoke row covers it either — `hostile 4` (smoke.py:35-36) runs at `bot_health=20`, i.e. the fight path.

The round-03 goal explicitly makes "question text matches the stub" a merge condition, and it does not.
findings.fix: Update the `idle` criterion in both brain.js:102 and laya/test/request.json:11 to the state the stub actually idles in, e.g. "The player is within 3 blocks and is moving, or a hostile mob is near but the bot has less than 6 health and the player is close: stand still and wait.", and extend the `follow` criterion with the caution case: "…or a hostile mob is near, the bot has less than 6 health and the player is more than 3 blocks away: walk back to the player." Optionally add a `dist 5 hurt hostile` row to smoke.py STATES so the table shows the caution case.

findings.title: Roam's hand-back wedges the tick: the bot freezes for good when a stroll ends just past 6 blocks
findings.body:
`roam.js:23` returns without touching the pathfinder when the bot is more than `HAND_BACK_DIST` (6) from the player, on the comment's assumption that "the next tick's brain answer will be follow". There is no next brain answer: `index.js:113` reuses `lastDecision` while `stateKey` is unchanged, and `perception.js:33` rounds `distance_to_player` to whole blocks. A stationary bot with a stationary player produces a byte-identical key forever, so the cached `roam` is re-dispatched every tick and `roam.js:23` hands the body back every tick. Nothing moves, so nothing changes the key.

Trigger (run against the real `createTicker` + real `stubBrain`, mock pathfinder):
```
d=1    action=roam calledBrain=true  setGoals=1   (GoalNear picked, r close to 6)
d=3    action=roam calledBrain=true  setGoals=1   (walking)
d=5.6  action=roam calledBrain=true  setGoals=1   (key "6", roam cached)
d=6.4  action=roam calledBrain=false setGoals=1   (goal reached, isMoving false, hand-back)
d=6.4  action=roam calledBrain=false setGoals=1
d=6.4  action=roam calledBrain=false setGoals=1   ... forever
```
A fresh `stubBrain.decide({distance_to_player: 6.4, player_moving: false})` returns `follow` — the bot is frozen only because the stale `roam` is never re-evaluated.

Reachability: `GoalNear(x, pp.y, z, 1)` lets the bot come to rest up to ~1 block beyond a point picked at `r` up to `ROAM_RADIUS=6`, so any stroll with `r > 5` that arrives from the far side of an obstacle, or on a block a step above the player's y (the distance at `roam.js:20` is 3-D), rests at 6.0-6.9. The arrival tick is exactly where consecutive distances are closest, so the previous tick's key is usually also "6" and the cache hits. The bot then stands still until the player moves, a hostile appears, or health/food changes — which is precisely the "bot looks dead" symptom the bead exists to remove, and it violates the acceptance criterion "player stands still -> the bot strolls".

The same wedge fires whenever the remote brain answers `roam` at any distance past 6 (the case round 01 defended this branch as a guard for): the guard itself is what stops the loop.

No test covers it. `roam.test.js:75-82` calls `roam()` directly at d=20 with a fresh ctx, so it never sees the cache; the new crossover test at `roam.test.js:94-119` jumps 5.5 -> 7, straddling the (6, 6.5) window where the rounded key stays 6.
findings.fix: Never let roam return without either moving the body or changing the state: raise `HAND_BACK_DIST` to 8 (the bead's own "never leaves 8"), so a bot resting at 6.4 picks a fresh GoalNear inside the envelope and walks back in, changing the key and letting the brain re-decide. Add a ticker-level test that runs three ticks with the bot parked at 6.4 after a cached roam and asserts either a second setGoal or a follow decision.

findings.title: bot/README.md still documents three brain actions and the old 3-block follow/idle thresholds
findings.body:
`bot/README.md:50-54` enumerates the brain's exclusive actions as `fight` / `follow` / `idle` with "`idle`: Player is close (<= 3 blocks)", and the behaviours table at `:61-63` says `follow` triggers at "> 3 blocks away" and `idle` at "Player within 3 blocks". After this change a still player at 1-6 blocks yields `roam`, and follow triggers at >3 only while the player is moving, >6 while standing still. All three lines are now wrong and `roam` has no row at all.

The README is the document the in-game acceptance check is read against — the bead says "log lines show action=roam", and an owner reading this README to run that check finds no documented `action=roam` and an idle trigger that states the opposite of what the bot does. The table is also the observation guide for the deployed bot, so the drift lands on a reader diagnosing the live server. Prose only — nothing breaks at runtime, and the bead's Files list does not name bot/README.md, so this is arguably deferrable.
findings.fix: Add a `roam` bullet and table row (trigger: player within 6 blocks and standing still, no hostile near; observe: stand still, bot strolls and never leaves ~8) and correct the `follow` and `idle` triggers to the moving/still split (>3 moving, >6 still).

findings.title: Duplicate stub test case: 'follows back once the stroll leaves the envelope' repeats lines 23-25 verbatim
findings.body:
`brain.test.js:32-34` asserts `stubBrain.decide({ distance_to_player: 7, player_moving: false })` equals follow — character-for-character the same call and expectation as `brain.test.js:23-25` ('follow wins over roam once the player is beyond the envelope (dist 7, still)'). It adds no coverage: deleting either one leaves the same set of mutants killed. (`:11-13` d=1 moving and `:35-37` d=2 moving are likewise near-duplicates, though those at least differ in distance.)

Against the project's smallest-diff rule this is test noise in a diff that is otherwise tightly scoped; it also makes the suite read as if two distinct envelope boundaries were pinned when only one is.
findings.fix: Delete `brain.test.js:32-34`, or repoint it at the boundary that is genuinely untested — a still player at d=6.4, the distance at which the cached-roam wedge in roam.js bites.
